TITLE: Investigating the Role of Dimensionality in Token Embedding Optimization
PROPOSAL: Examine the impact of varying embedding dimensions on the performance and convergence speed of Textual Inversion (TI) for personalizing subject images in the Berkeley Segmentation Dataset (BSDS500) and State Farm Distracted Driver Detection dataset (D3D). Compare TI's performance with an ablated version of the model where embedding dimensions are fixed at their original, low value. Use mean squared error (MSE) and feature similarity index (FSI) as evaluation metrics to measure image fidelity and similarity to the original subjects.
CONTROLS: Fixed embedding dimension model, ablated in target domains of BSDS500 and D3D using across-cut contrastive loss.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Increased dimensionality will lead to more accurate image renderings and faster convergence, but may sacrificing some model interpretability. 

Some expected failure modes include: redundancy of additional dimensions, computational overhead for dense embedding spaces.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Refining Dimensionality Analysis and Adding Baselines
PROPOSAL: Refine the proposal from turn 1 by incorporating two additional baselines for comparison: (1) DreamBooth, parameter fine-tuning method for efficiency and high-quality images, and (2) a dimensionality-reduced version of TI where the internal dimensionality is decreased to match the fixed, low-value embedding dimension. Also, evaluate TI for specific sub-tasks within personalized text-to-image generation, such as subject-driven image generation and artistic style transfer using COCO-dataset for images and a pre-existing style transfer dataset for abstract artistic styles.
CONTROLS: Three controls: original TI, ablated fixed dimension, and DreamBooth
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: TI with increased dimensionality will show improved performance, but will remain inferior to DreamBooth in terms of quality and sometime will even degrade for specific style transfer or text-driven generation sub-tasks.

TITLE: Unsupervised Training for Textual Inversion
PROPOSAL: Develop an unsupervised training method for Textual Inversion (TI), leveraging self-supervision and contrastive learning to optimize the token embedding space without requiring explicit labels or user-provided images. Use a self-supervised training setup where the model predicts the original prompt from corrupted or noisy input. Evaluate this unsupervised TI approach for its effectiveness in adapting to distinct styles and preserving the AI model's capacity to generate diverse candid images in the uncontrolled manner, especially in an artistic variety using a dataset that would presumably be already relatively photorealistic but diverse in art style such as the AIC25 dataset
CONTROLS: Supervised TI, random initialization
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This unsupervised approach could simplify the targeted personalization of the image rendering, albeit efficiency could be affected by the utilization of necessarily parallelized partial optimisation routines.

TITLE: Photorealism and Identity Preservation in Textual Inversion
PROPOSAL: Assess the photorealism and identity preservation of images generated using Textual Inversion (TI) in comparison to those generated using DreamBooth, a state-of-the-art parameter fine-tuning method. Use a dataset of diverse, high-quality faces with varying expressions, poses, and backgrounds (e.g., CelebA, LSUN), and evaluate the generated images using metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and human evaluation. Investigate whether TI's photorealism and identity preservation can be improved through augmentation of the target images and/or exploring different configuration for the text encoder and decoder.
CONTROLS: Original TI, DreamBooth
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: TI may struggle to match DreamBooth's photorealism and identity preservation due to its optimization dynamics. However, with appropriate dataset augmentation and model configurations, TI can demonstrate superior quality for certain types of images (e.g., abstract artistic styles).

TITLE: Hybrid Model with(concatenated) Conditional Normalization
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hybrid model that combines the strengths of Textual Inversion and parameter fine-tuning methods by incorporating a conditional normalization layer. This layer modulates the output of the text encoder based on the learned token embeddings, thereby allowing the model to adapt to different image styles and attributes. Evaluate the hybrid model's performance on various personalized text-to-image generation tasks, including face personalization and artistic style transfer, using datasets like CelebA and COCO.
CONTROLS: Original TI, DreamBooth
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hybrid model will demonstrate improved photorealism, identity preservation, and adaptability to diverse image styles and attributes, overcoming some of the limitations of Textual Inversion alone.

TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Prompt Engineering on Textual Inversion
PROPOSAL: Explore the impact of prompt engineering techniques on the performance of Textual Inversion (TI), including methods for generating more informative and targeted prompts. Evaluate the effectiveness of manually crafted prompts, as well as automated methods for generating prompts, such as using generative models or ranking candidate prompts based on their relevance to the target concept. Assess the impact of prompt engineering on the convergence speed, accuracy, and fidelity of images generated by TI using a dataset of diverse, high-quality images (e.g., COCO).
CONTROLS: Original TI, original DreamBooth
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Prompt engineering techniques can significantly improve the performance of TI, leading to faster convergence, higher accuracy, and improved fidelity of generated images. However, the effectiveness of these techniques may vary depending on the specific dataset and target concepts.

TITLE: Scalable Textual Inversion for Large-Scale Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a scalable and computationally efficient Textual Inversion (TI) framework for generating large-scale images, capable of handling thousands of target concepts and complex images. Utilize distributed training and parallel processing techniques to speed up the optimization process, while maintaining the fidelity and photorealism of the generated images. Evaluate the performance of the scalable TI framework on a large-scale image generation dataset (e.g., ImageNet) and compare it with existing state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: Original TI, distributed version of TI
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The scalable TI framework will demonstrate significant improvements in terms of computational efficiency, allowing for the generation of large-scale images at a faster rate without compromising on fidelity and photorealism. However, its performance may depend on the specific hardware and software configurations used for distributed training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Optimizer's Role in Embedding Optimization
PROPOSAL: Experiment with different optimizers (e.g., Adam, SGD, L-BFGS-B) during the embedding optimization process in Textual Inversion and evaluate their effects on convergence speed, stability, and representation capacity. Compare the performance of the learned embeddings on a standard downstream task, like image synthesis, using the pre-trained text encoder and decoder architecture from DALL-E.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments using the default Adam optimizer, ablation experiments where the learning rate is fixed or decayed, and control experiments with the original Textual Inversion implementation.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (considering 2 baselines and 4 ablations)
PREDICTION: Optimizers with a high level of adaptivity, such as Adam, will lead to better convergence speeds and lower representation capacity compared to optimizers like L-BFGS-B, but could also affect the stability of the optimization process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visualizing Embedding Space Geometry via t-SNE
PROPOSAL: Use t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) to visualize the geometric structure of the learned token embeddings in Textual Inversion on a standard dataset, such as the LSUN bedrooms dataset. Compare the visualization results to the original pre-trained vocabulary embeddings and investigate their differences, highlighting clusters or groupings that may be related to learned concepts.
CONTROLS: Control experiments to compare the visualization results using different perplexity values for t-SNE, as well as experiments to compare the performance of t-SNE with other dimensionality reduction techniques, like PCA.
COST: 5 GPU-hours (considering 2 ablations and 1 control)
PREDICTION: t-SNE will reveal complex clusters related to learned concepts, and dimensionality reduction will have a significant impact on the visual representation of the embedding space, effectively highlighting the geometric properties of TI's internal representation that are essential for interpretation and understanding.

TITLE: Hierarchical Embedding Representation for Personalized Generation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the efficacy of learning a hierarchical representation for the target embedding in Textual Inversion, which captures both low-level and high-level semantic properties of the concepts. This can be achieved by designing a nested embedding space where the inner embeddings capture the basic properties of the concepts (e.g., colors, textures), and the outer embeddings capture the more abstract properties (e.g., composition, context).
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments using the standard Textual Inversion approach and ablation experiments to investigate the impact of hierarchical representation on the learned embeddings and the quality of the generated images.
